title.zh: 卷26 志一 天文一 天象地体里差
title.en: Volume 26 Treatises 1: Astronomy 1, Celestial Phenomena, Earth Shape, and Terrestrial Distances
title.raw: 卷26 志一 天文一 天象地体里差

sentences.zh: 歷代天文誌，自《史記·天官書》後，唯晉、隋兩誌，備述天體、儀象、星占，唐、宋加詳，皆未盡也。

translations.literal: Astronomical treatises of successive dynasties, after the Records of the Grand Historian's Treatise on the Heavenly Offices, only the Jin and Sui treatises fully describe celestial bodies, instruments, and star divination; the Tang and Song added detail, yet none is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic astronomy monographs after Sima Qian's Heavenly Offices are fully descriptive only in the Jin and Sui versions; Tang and Song expanded them, but gaps remain.

sentences.zh: 至元，景測益精明，占候較密，然疆宇所囿，聲教未宏，齊政窺璣，尚多略焉。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan, instrumental observation grew more precise and prognostication denser, yet the realm they enclosed and cultural sway they spread were not broad; aligning government with the celestial pivot still left much omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan observers refined instruments and tightened forecasts, but within a limited empire their cosmological governance still fell short.

sentences.zh: 有清統一區夏，聖聖相承。

translations.literal: The Qing unified All-under-Heaven, sage succeeding sage.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing unified China, one sage emperor following another.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親釐象數，究極精微，前後制新儀七，測日月星辰，則窮極分秒；

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor personally rectified numerology and celestial phenomena, penetrating the utmost subtlety; before and after he devised seven new instruments; in measuring sun, moon, and stars he exhausted fractions of seconds;
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi emperor personally mastered calendrical astronomy, devised seven new instruments, and measured the sun, moon, and stars to the second.

sentences.zh: 度輿圖經緯，則穹歷幅隕。

translations.literal: in surveying carriage routes' longitude and latitude, the vault's calendar and the dome's chart.
translations.idiomatic: In surveying terrestrial longitude and latitude he mapped the heavens' span across the sky.

sentences.zh: 世宗復以歲久積差，準監臣改用橢圓術。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor again, because long years had accumulated discrepancy, ordered supervising officials to adopt the elliptical method.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng, seeing accumulated error over the years, had supervising astronomers adopt elliptical theory.

sentences.zh: 高宗又以舊記星紀，間有疏漏，御製璣衡撫辰儀，重加測候。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor again, because old star records had occasional gaps, personally made the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and took new observations.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong, finding gaps in older star catalogs, built the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and remeasured the sky.

sentences.zh: 迨平定回疆及兩金川，復令重度裏差，增入時憲。

translations.literal: When the Muslim borderlands and the Two Jinchuan were pacified, he again ordered remeasurement of li-cha and added the results to the Time Constitution calendar.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Xinjiang and the two Jinchuan campaigns, he ordered li-cha remeasured and entered into the Shixian calendar.

sentences.zh: 理明數確，器精法密，自古以來，所未有也。

translations.literal: Principles clear, numbers exact, instruments refined, methods dense—from antiquity there has never been the like.
translations.idiomatic: Clarity of principle, exactitude of number, refinement of instrument, and density of method were unmatched in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 今為天文誌，備載推驗之法，其天象昭垂，見於歷朝實錄及所司載記者，亦悉書之。

translations.literal: Now for the Astronomy Treatise we fully record methods of computation and verification; celestial phenomena manifest overhead, as seen in successive dynasties' Veritable Records and the offices' records, are also all written.
translations.idiomatic: This Astronomy Treatise records computational methods and every celestial phenomenon noted in dynastic Veritable Records and observatory logs.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年以後，國史無徵，則從闕焉。

translations.literal: After Qianlong year 60 the National History has no testimony, and those years are therefore omitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianlong 60 the Veritable Records offer no material, so the account stops there.

sentences.zh: 天象地體裏差

translations.literal: Celestial Phenomena, Earth's Form, and Li-Cha
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Phenomena, Earth's Form, and Li-Cha

sentences.zh: 天象歷象考成天象篇云：「《楚辭·天問》曰：『圜則九重，孰營度之？

translations.literal: Celestial Phenomena and Calendrical Phenomena, Compilation of Heavenly Phenomena says: "The Chu Ci, Heavenly Questions, says: 'Round then ninefold — who planned and measured it?
translations.idiomatic: The Compilation of Heavenly Phenomena quotes the Chu Ci Heavenly Questions: "The heavens are ninefold round — who designed and measured them?

sentences.zh: 』後世歷家，謂天有十二重，非天實有如許重數，蓋言日月星辰運轉於天，各有所行之道，即楚辭所謂圜也。

translations.literal: " Later calendar specialists said heaven has twelve layers; heaven does not truly have so many layers — it speaks of sun, moon, and stars revolving in heaven, each with its own path — that is what the Chu Ci calls round.
translations.idiomatic: Later astronomers spoke of twelve celestial spheres not as literal shells but as the separate paths of sun, moon, and stars — the "round" of the Chu Ci.

sentences.zh: 欲明諸圜之理，必詳諸圜之動，欲考諸圜之動，必以至靜不動者準之，然後得其盈縮。

translations.literal: To clarify the principles of the spheres one must detail their motions; to examine their motions one must take what is utterly still and unmoving as standard — then one obtains their waxing and waning.
translations.idiomatic: To understand celestial spheres one must study their motion against an absolutely fixed reference; only then can expansion and contraction be calculated.

sentences.zh: 蓋天道靜專者也，天行動直者也。

translations.literal: For the Way of Heaven is still and dedicated; heaven's motion is active and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way is still and single-minded; its motion is active and direct.

sentences.zh: 至靜者自有一天，與地相為表裏，故群動者運於其間而不息。

translations.literal: The utterly still has a heaven of its own, inner and outer garment with earth, hence the many movers operate within it without cease.
translations.idiomatic: An absolutely fixed heaven pairs with earth as inner and outer; all moving bodies wheel within it unceasingly.

sentences.zh: 若無至靜者以驗至動，則聖人亦無所成其能矣。

translations.literal: If there were no utterly still by which to verify the utmost motion, the sage would have no means to accomplish his skill.
translations.idiomatic: Without a fixed frame against which to measure motion, even the sage could not perfect his art.

sentences.zh: 人恒在地面測天，而七政之行無不可得者，正為以靜驗動故也。

translations.literal: Humans always measure heaven from earth's surface, yet the seven luminaries' motions can all be obtained — precisely because still verifies motion.
translations.idiomatic: Observers stand on earth yet can chart the seven luminaries because motion is measured against what does not move.

sentences.zh: 「十二重天，最外者為至靜不動；

translations.literal: "The twelve-layer heaven — outermost is utterly still and unmoving;
translations.idiomatic: "Of the twelve spheres, the outermost is absolutely fixed;

sentences.zh: 次為宗動，南北極赤道所由分也。

translations.literal: next is the primum mobile, where north and south poles and the equator are divided;
translations.idiomatic: next the primum mobile, which defines the poles and equator;

sentences.zh: 次為南北歲差；

translations.literal: next is north-south precession;
translations.idiomatic: next north-south precession;

sentences.zh: 次為東西歲差；

translations.literal: next is east-west precession;
translations.idiomatic: next east-west precession;

sentences.zh: 此二重天，其動甚微，歷家姑置之而不論焉。

translations.literal: these two heavens move very slightly; calendar specialists provisionally set them aside and do not discuss them.
translations.idiomatic: these two spheres move imperceptibly and astronomers usually ignore them.

sentences.zh: 次為三垣二十八宿，經星行焉。

translations.literal: next are the Three Enclosures and Twenty-eight Mansions, through which the fixed stars pass;
translations.idiomatic: next the Three Enclosures and Twenty-eight Mansions where fixed stars travel;

sentences.zh: 次為填星所行；

translations.literal: next that where Saturn moves;
translations.idiomatic: next Saturn's sphere;

sentences.zh: 次為歲星所行；

translations.literal: next where Jupiter moves;
translations.idiomatic: next Jupiter's;

sentences.zh: 次為熒惑所行；

translations.literal: next where Mars moves;
translations.idiomatic: next Mars's;

sentences.zh: 次則太陽所行，黃道是也。

translations.literal: next where the Sun moves — the ecliptic;
translations.idiomatic: next the sun's ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 次為太白所行；

translations.literal: next where Venus moves;
translations.idiomatic: next Venus's;

sentences.zh: 次為辰星所行；

translations.literal: next where Mercury moves;
translations.idiomatic: next Mercury's;

sentences.zh: 最內者則太陰所行，白道是也。

translations.literal: innermost where the Moon moves — the white path.
translations.idiomatic: innermost the moon's white path.

sentences.zh: 要以去地之遠近而為諸天之內外，然所以知去地之遠近者，則又從諸曜之掩食及行度之遲疾而得之。

translations.literal: Essentials: by distance from earth as inner and outer of the heavens; yet how one knows distance from earth is again from the luminaries' occultations and eclipses and from degrees' slowness and speed.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far are ranked by distance from earth, known from mutual occultations, eclipses, and relative speed in degrees.

sentences.zh: 蓋凡為所掩食者必在上，而掩之食之者必在下。

translations.literal: For whatever is occulted or eclipsed must be above; what occults or eclipses must be below.
translations.idiomatic: The body eclipsed lies above; the eclipser below.

sentences.zh: 月體能蔽日光而日為之食，是日遠月近之徵也。

translations.literal: The moon's body can obscure sunlight and the sun is eclipsed — a sign the sun is far and the moon near.
translations.idiomatic: The moon blocks the sun in eclipse, proving the sun farther than the moon.

sentences.zh: 月能掩食五星，而月與五星又能掩食恒星，是五星高於月而卑於恒星也。

translations.literal: The moon can occult the five stars, and moon and five stars can occult fixed stars — the five stars are higher than the moon yet lower than fixed stars.
translations.idiomatic: The moon occults the five planets; moon and planets occult fixed stars — planets stand above the moon but below the fixed stars.

sentences.zh: 五星又能互相掩食，是五星各有遠近也。

translations.literal: The five stars can also mutually occult one another — each has its own near and far.
translations.idiomatic: The five planets also occult one another, each at a different distance.

sentences.zh: 「又宗動天以渾灝之氣挈諸天左旋，其行甚速。

translations.literal: "Also the primum mobile heaven, with vast qi, carries all heavens in left rotation; its motion is very swift.
translations.idiomatic: "The primum mobile, by vast ethereal force, drags all spheres in daily rotation — very fast.

sentences.zh: 故近宗動天者，左旋速而右移之度遲。

translations.literal: Hence near the primum mobile heaven, left rotation is swift and rightward shift slow.
translations.idiomatic: Near it, daily rotation is fast and apparent retrograde motion slow.

sentences.zh: 漸遠宗動天，則左旋較遲而右移之度轉速。

translations.literal: Gradually farther from the primum mobile, left rotation is slower and rightward shift faster.
translations.idiomatic: Farther out, daily rotation slows and retrograde motion quickens.

sentences.zh: 今右移之度，惟恒星最遲，土木次之，火又次之。

translations.literal: Now for rightward shift: only fixed stars are slowest, Saturn and Jupiter next, Mars again next.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde speed ranks fixed stars slowest, then Saturn and Jupiter, then Mars.

sentences.zh: 日、金、水較速而月最速，是又以次而近之證也。

translations.literal: Sun, Venus, and Mercury are faster and the moon fastest — again proof by successive nearness.
translations.idiomatic: The sun, Venus, and Mercury move faster; the moon fastest — another proof of nearness.

translations.literal: " (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.)

sentences.zh: 考成後編日躔歷理云：「西法自多祿某以至第谷，立為本天高卑、本輪、均輪諸說，近世刻白爾、噶西尼等，又以本天為橢圓。

translations.literal: Post-Compilation Daily Solar Motion Treatise says: "Western method from Ptolemy to Tycho established deferent heights, epicycle, and eccentric theories; recent Kepler, Cassini, and others took the deferent as an ellipse.
translations.idiomatic: The Daily Solar Motion Treatise notes: from Ptolemy through Tycho came deferents, epicycles, and eccentrics; Kepler and Cassini made the deferent elliptical.

sentences.zh: 」月離歷理云：「自西人創為橢圓之法，日距月天最高有遠近，則太陰本天心有進退。

translations.literal: "Lunar Distance Treatise says: "Since Westerners created the ellipse method, the sun's distance from the lunar heaven at apogee has near and far, and the moon's deferent center has advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The Lunar Distance Treatise adds: elliptical theory makes the sun's distance from the lunar sphere vary and the lunar deferent center oscillate.

sentences.zh: 地心與天心相距，兩心差有大小。

translations.literal: Earth center and heaven center are apart; the two centers' difference has magnitude.
translations.idiomatic: Earth center and celestial center diverge by a measurable interval.

sentences.zh: 」合觀諸論，天象備矣。

translations.literal: " Viewing all discussions together, celestial phenomena are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, these accounts complete the picture of celestial phenomena.

sentences.zh: 恒星天無地半徑差及次輪消息，故誌土星以下七天距地心數，著考測之詳焉。

translations.literal: The fixed-star heaven has no earth-radius difference or secondary-cycle variation, so the treatise records from Saturn downward the seven heavens' distances from earth center, detailing survey particulars.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed stars show no parallax or epicycle variation; below Saturn the treatise lists each planet's distance from earth's center from survey data.

sentences.zh: 諸天距地心數：

translations.literal: Distances of the heavens from earth center:
translations.idiomatic: Distances from earth center:

sentences.zh: 土星最高一十一又一百零四萬二千六百分之三十五萬二千六百日天半徑；

translations.literal: Saturn at highest: eleven and 1,042,626/352,606 solar radii;
translations.idiomatic: Saturn apogee: 11 + 1,042,626/352,606 solar radii;

sentences.zh: 木星最高六又一百九十二萬九千四百八十分之一百三十萬五千九百日天半徑；

translations.literal: Jupiter at highest: six and 1,929,408/1,305,590 solar radii;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter apogee: 6 + 1,929,408/1,305,590 solar radii;

sentences.zh: 火星最高二又六百三十萬二千七百五十分之五百五十五萬二千二百五十日天半徑；

translations.literal: Mars at highest: two and 6,302,705/5,552,250 solar radii;
translations.idiomatic: Mars apogee: 2 + 6,302,705/5,552,250 solar radii;

sentences.zh: 日均輪術最高一千一百六十二地半徑，橢圓術最高二萬零九百七十五地半徑；

translations.literal: Sun — mean epicycle method at highest: 1,162 earth radii; ellipse method at highest: 20,975 earth radii;
translations.idiomatic: Sun: mean epicycle 1,162 earth radii; ellipse 20,975 earth radii;

sentences.zh: 金星最高高於日一千萬分日天半徑之七百五十四萬五千六百四十四，最下下於日如之；

translations.literal: Venus at highest above the sun: 7,545,644/10,000,000 of a solar radius; at lowest below the sun by the same amount;
translations.idiomatic: Venus apogee: 7,545,644/10,000,000 solar radius above the sun; perigee equally below;

sentences.zh: 水星最高高於日一千萬分日天半徑之四百五十三萬二千一百五十五，最下下於日如之；

translations.literal: Mercury at highest above the sun: 4,532,155/10,000,000 of a solar radius; at lowest below the sun by the same amount;
translations.idiomatic: Mercury apogee: 4,532,155/10,000,000 solar radius above the sun; perigee equally below;

sentences.zh: 月均輪術最高朔望時五十八又百分之一十六地半徑，橢圓術最高六十三又百分之七十七地半徑。

translations.literal: Moon — mean epicycle method at highest at new and full moon: fifty-eight and 16/100 earth radii; ellipse method at highest: sixty-three and 77/100 earth radii.
translations.idiomatic: Moon: mean epicycle 58.16 earth radii at syzygy; ellipse 63.77 earth radii.

sentences.zh: 地體渾天家謂天包地如卵裹黃，內經：「黃帝曰：『地之為下否乎？

translations.literal: Earth's body — armillary-sphere cosmologists say heaven wraps earth like an egg wrapping the yolk; Inner Classic: "Yellow Emperor said: 'Is earth truly below?'
translations.idiomatic: On earth's form: armillary cosmologists say heaven encloses earth like a shell around a yolk. The Inner Classic records: "The Yellow Emperor asked, 'Is earth truly beneath us?'

sentences.zh: 』岐伯曰：『地為人之下，太虛之中也。

translations.literal: Qibo said: 'Earth is below man, within the Great Void.'
translations.idiomatic: Qibo answered, 'Earth lies below humanity, suspended in the Great Void.'

sentences.zh: 』曰：『憑乎？

translations.literal: He said: 'Resting on what?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 'On what does it rest?'

sentences.zh: 』曰：『大義舉之也。

translations.literal: He said: 'The Great Principle lifts it.'
translations.idiomatic: Qibo said, 'The Great Principle holds it up.'"

sentences.zh: 』」大戴禮：「單居離問於曾子曰：『天圓而地方，誠有之乎？

translations.literal: Great Dai Rites: "Danju Li asked Zengzi: 'Heaven round and earth square — is it truly so?'
translations.idiomatic: The Great Dai Rites records Danju Li asking Zengzi, 'Heaven is round and earth square — is that true?'

sentences.zh: 』曾子曰：『如誠天圓而地方，則是四角之不掩也。

translations.literal: Zengzi said: 'If heaven were truly round and earth square, the four corners would not meet.'
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi replied, 'If heaven were round and earth square, the corners would not align.'

sentences.zh: 參嘗聞諸夫子曰：「天道曰圓，地道曰方。

translations.literal: I once heard from the Master: "Heaven's Way is called round; Earth's Way is called square."'"
translations.idiomatic: I heard the Master say, "Heaven's Way is called round; earth's Way is called square."'

sentences.zh: 」』」宋儒邵子曰：「天何依？

translations.literal: Song Neo-Confucian Shao Yong said: "On what does heaven rely? On earth;
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yong of the Song asked, "On what does heaven rely? On earth.

sentences.zh: 依乎地；

translations.literal: It relies on earth;
translations.idiomatic: It relies on earth;

sentences.zh: 地何附？

translations.literal: On what does earth attach?
translations.idiomatic: On what does earth attach?

sentences.zh: 附乎天。

translations.literal: To heaven.
translations.idiomatic: To heaven.

sentences.zh: 天地何所依附？

translations.literal: On what do heaven and earth mutually attach?
translations.idiomatic: On what do heaven and earth attach to each other?

sentences.zh: 自相依附。

translations.literal: They attach to each other.
translations.idiomatic: They attach to each other.

sentences.zh: 自相依附，天依形，地附氣。

translations.literal: Mutually attaching — heaven by form, earth by qi."
translations.idiomatic: Mutually attaching: heaven by form, earth by qi."

sentences.zh: 」程子曰：「據日景以三萬里為中，若有窮，然有至一邊已及一萬五千里，而天地之運蓋如初。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi said: "By the sun's shadow, thirty thousand li as center — it seems bounded, yet when one side has already reached fifteen thousand li, heaven and earth's motion is as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi said, "By gnomon shadow, thirty thousand li marks the center; it seems finite, yet at fifteen thousand li on one side heaven and earth still move as before.

sentences.zh: 然則中者亦時中耳。

translations.literal: Then the center is also a temporal center."
translations.idiomatic: The center is only the center for a given moment."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「今人所定天體，只是且以眼定，視所極處不見，遂以為盡。

translations.literal: He also said: "What people now fix as the celestial body is only by the eye — where vision ends they take as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "People define the heavens only by sight — where the eye stops, they call that the edge.

sentences.zh: 然向曾有於海上見南極下有大星十，則今所見天體蓋未定。

translations.literal: Yet once at sea one saw ten large stars below the south pole; today's fixed celestial body is therefore unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at sea ten bright stars appeared south of the pole, so our celestial map remains uncertain.

sentences.zh: 日月升降，不過三萬里中，然而中國只到鄯善、沙車，已是一萬五千里。

translations.literal: Sun and moon rise and set only within thirty thousand li at center; yet China reaches only Shanshan and Yarkand — already fifteen thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon move within thirty thousand li of center, while China reaches only Shanshan and Yarkand — half that span.

sentences.zh: 若就彼觀日，尚只是三萬里中也。

translations.literal: Viewed from there the sun would still lie within thirty thousand li of center.
translations.idiomatic: From there the sun would still appear at the same central distance.

sentences.zh: 伯淳在澤州，嘗三次食韭黃，始食懷州韭，次食澤州，次食并州，則知數百里間，氣候已爭三月矣。

translations.literal: Bochun at Zezhou once ate chive shoots three times — first Huai chives, then Ze chives, then Bing chives — and knew that within a few hundred li climate already differed by three months.
translations.idiomatic: At Zezhou, Bochun ate chives three times — from Huai, Ze, and Bing — and found climate three months apart within hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 若都以此差之，則須爭半歲。

translations.literal: If one extrapolated by that difference, it would amount to half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolated, the difference would reach half a year.

sentences.zh: 如是，則有在此冬至、在彼夏至者，只是一般為冬夏而已。

translations.literal: Thus there could be winter solstice here and summer solstice there — only the names winter and summer would differ."
translations.idiomatic: One place could have winter solstice while another had summer solstice — merely opposite seasons."

sentences.zh: 」朱子天問註云：「天之形圓如彈丸，其運轉者亦無形質，但如勁風之旋。

translations.literal: " (closing quotation mark in the source.) Zhu Xi's commentary on Heavenly Questions says: "Heaven's form is round like a pellet; what rotates also has no substance, but is like a fierce wind's whirl.
translations.idiomatic: (closing quotation mark in the source.) Zhu Xi's Heavenly Questions commentary: heaven is round like a pellet; its rotation has no solid body, only a whirl of fierce wind.

sentences.zh: 地則氣之渣滓聚成形質者，但以其束於勁風旋轉之中，故得以兀然浮空甚久而不墮耳。

translations.literal: Earth is the dregs of qi gathered into form, but because it is bound within the fierce wind's rotation it can alone float in the void long without falling."
translations.idiomatic: Earth is condensed qi, held aloft in that whirl so long that it seems to float without falling."

sentences.zh: 」西人謂地體渾圓，四面皆有人，冬夏互異，晝夜相反，與內經、戴記及宋儒之言若合符節。

translations.literal: Westerners say earth's body is perfectly round, with people on all four sides; winter and summer differ and day and night reverse — matching the Inner Classic, the Dai Rites, and Song Confucians as if tallying seal and notch.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners hold the earth a perfect sphere with inhabitants on every side, opposite seasons and reversed day and night — matching the Inner Classic, Dai Rites, and Song masters.

sentences.zh: 惟得其所差之數，則各殊之故，皆可豫知，不致詫為失行而生飾說矣。
